newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-SUGAR RAY LEONARD SAYS HE MAY FIGHT AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-SUGAR RAY LEONARD SAYS HE MAY FIGHT AGAIN.

text.p: Sugar Ray Leonard said Thursday that he has not retired from boxing, despite what he said after receiving a brutal beating from Hector Camacho five days earlier.

Leonard, who returned to the ring after a six-year absence only to be humiliated by the light-hitting Camacho last Saturday, told the ESPN sports cable television network that he plans to fight again.

"I'm not retired," Leonard told "Up Close" show host Chris Myers. "I know people say, 'Ray, you're crazy, you're disillusioned, and you're really searching for an uncatchable dream.' That is not the case. I know what I'm capable of doing."

The 40-year-old five-time former champion was stopped in the fifth round last Saturday. Leonard said he had injured his right leg in training and said that he had taken four shots of novocaine for the injury right before the fight.
After the bout, Leonard had said: "My career is definitely over for me in the ring. I'm through."

But he said on Saturday: "Yes, I would fight again. I want to, I'm going to. To say will I go back and try to fight a champion right away? No, I'm going to take it easy and go through a series of tuneups to get myself back where I was two months ago."
Leonard, who won world titles in five different weight divisions, has a 36-3-1 record. He has lost his last two fights.

Leonard was knocked down on the seat of his pants early in the fifth round and Camacho followed up by pinning him against the ropes with a flurry of 10 unanswered punches before the referee stopped the onslaught.
"The referee did the right thing," Leonard said after the fight. "There was no sense in my getting hurt."
Leonard rose to prominence by winning a gold medal at the 1976 Olympics in Montreal.

He was victorious in memorable battles with Roberto Duran, Tommy Hearns and Marvin Hagler before a detached retina derailed his career. His only losses were to Duran and Terry Norris and he fought to an epic draw with Hearns in 1989.
